content:
Doc purpose (notes to self / shared working space)
- Capture kickoff decisions + open questions for the “hardware tuning profiles pack” initiative.
- Early list of candidate knobs (what we think is safe to freeze vs keep adaptive).
- Early hypotheses on H100 vs L40S differences (and what we expect to tune).
- This is not a spec. The Confluence docs will be the source of truth once stabilized.

Kickoff meeting
- Date: 2025-11-06
- Attendees (partial): Talia (EPL), Hiro (kernels), Sofia (scheduling), Ethan (schema/guardrails), Benji (loader/overrides), Irene (fleet/rollout), Rina + Claire (bench), Neha (SRE), Maya (Applied ML)

High-level framing
- We keep seeing “almost good” defaults that regress on one SKU or one workload class (especially long-context streaming + high concurrency).
- Goal: ship curated, versioned runtime configuration profiles per GPU SKU (H100, L40S first; B200 gated/experimental).
- The pack must be:
  - Safe-by-default with explicit workload envelope
  - Measurable (bench harness + standardized report)
  - Rollout-friendly (canary gates, staged by pool/region)
  - Debuggable (metrics: selected profile, override source, key knobs)
  - Reversible quickly (per-pool disable + fallback)

Non-goals (for initial release)
- No new kernels from scratch.
- No API surface changes (we can add logs/metrics/debug endpoints, but no customer-visible breaking changes).
- No bespoke customer-by-customer tuning baked into the pack (Support/Solutions can layer overrides, but the pack must remain broadly applicable).

Target SKUs (phase 1)
- H100 (SXM + PCIe variants in fleet; assume we’ll need guardrails for clocks / HBM size variance)
- L40S (memory constrained vs H100; target “cost-sensitive + reliable” envelope)
- B200 (experimental, behind feature flag, partial fleet access; explicit fallback plan required)

Success metrics (directional targets; to be formalized in Confluence)
- Latency: improve or hold p50, avoid p95/p99 regressions beyond agreed thresholds.
- Throughput: tokens/sec improvements on representative workloads.
- Cost: improved token/$ under typical utilization.
- Stability: fewer OOMs, fewer tail spikes, fewer canary incidents attributable to mis-tuned runtime configs.
- Operator experience: oncall can identify what profile is active and disable/rollback within minutes.

Decision log (rough)
1) Ship H100 + L40S profiles first; B200 is experimental + opt-in.
2) Profiles should be versioned independently but pinned/validated against runtime versions (compat matrix).
3) Override order must be explicit and testable:
   - runtime defaults < profile pack defaults < fleet/pool defaults < deployment overrides (helm/env) < per-route overrides (if supported) < emergency kill switch
   - Need one “emergency disable profiles” toggle per pool.
4) We will define a workload matrix and publish “expected behavior” not “guarantees” (Docs wording: no accidental SLAs).

Workload realism notes (from Maya / Applied ML)
- Include a mix of:
  - Short prompts + long prompts
  - Tool-calling-ish patterns (structured output; function call token shapes)
  - Streaming vs non-streaming
  - Prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy distributions
- Avoid overfitting to microbenchmarks; use microbench only as explanatory signals.

Candidate knobs (brain dump)

A) Scheduler / batching / backpressure
- Continuous batching enable/disable and batching window
  - max_batch_size tokens
  - max_batch_delay_ms
  - separate prefill/decode queues? (or fairness knobs)
- Prefill vs decode fairness
  - prefill_priority_weight
  - decode_priority_weight
  - starvation protection thresholds
  - max_prefill_concurrency
- Queue/backpressure
  - max_queue_depth
  - queue_reject_threshold
  - admission control per route/tier
- Streaming behavior
  - chunk size / token emission cadence (trade-off CPU vs latency)
  - max_streaming_connections per worker
- CPU-side runtime settings (thread pools)
  - io_threads
  - scheduler_threads
  - tokenization threads (if relevant in runtime process)

Safety notes:
- Sofia: knobs that change tail latency behavior should be “bounded” and have guardrails (e.g., never allow decode starvation).
- Neha: need rollback threshold suggestions for p95 spikes; define SRE-ready alerting.

B) Kernel selection + attention implementation toggles
- Kernel auto-select heuristic inputs
  - seq_len buckets (prefill length vs decode length)
  - batch size buckets
  - kv-cache layout assumptions
- Attention path toggles
  - flash-attn variants (if multiple)
  - fused vs unfused paths
- Quantization compatibility
  - allowlist/denylist specific kernels under int8/fp8 modes (avoid silent perf regressions)

Safety notes:
- Hiro: prefer “choose between existing stable kernels” rather than “force a single kernel always.”
- Yuki (via Hiro): need a place in schema to express “heuristic policy,” not just fixed values.

C) KV cache / memory behavior
- KV cache budget
  - fixed budget (%) of HBM
  - per-request kv limit
  - eviction policy toggles (if available)
- Fragmentation mitigation
  - pre-allocation strategy
  - arena size
  - periodic defrag / reuse settings (if supported)
- OOM guardrails
  - hard stop before CUDA OOM (reject vs degrade)
  - safe fallback: reduce batch/disable certain optimizations

Safety notes:
- L40S is where we expect most value from guardrails; “don’t OOM” beats “maximize throughput.”

D) Collectives / multi-GPU (only where applicable)
- NCCL knobs (only if we run multi-GPU tensor parallel / pipeline parallel in some pools)
  - algo selection (ring/tree)
  - channel counts
  - p2p enable
- Topology awareness
  - PCIe vs NVLink differences

Open question: do we want SKU profiles to include topology sub-variants (e.g., H100-SXM vs H100-PCIe)? Or keep one H100 profile and let the loader refine based on detected interconnect? Lean: single profile + “capability flags” to branch.

E) Observability + debug
- Export metrics:
  - selected_profile_name
  - selected_profile_version
  - override_source (default/profile/pool/deployment/env/route)
  - key knob values as labels or debug endpoint output (avoid high-cardinality)
- Startup logs:
  - runtime version
  - profile pack version
  - compat matrix check result

Early hypotheses: H100 vs L40S (what we expect to tune)

H100 (goal: maximize throughput while holding tail latency)
- Likely can run more aggressive continuous batching windows (lower relative overhead).
- More headroom for larger KV cache budgets; less OOM risk.
- Kernel selection should bucket by seq length more aggressively (flash/fused benefits for mid-long prefill).
- Tail latency risk areas:
  - prefill-heavy arrivals can starve decode if fairness is off
  - streaming stability under high concurrency (CPU thread contention / scheduling)

L40S (goal: reliability + predictable cost; avoid memory pathologies)
- Memory is the limiting factor; long-context runs trigger KV growth quickly.
- Expect smaller KV cache budget cap + earlier admission control.
- Prefer conservative batching defaults; “more batching” can push us into fragmentation + OOM.
- Kernel selection may need to prefer lower memory overhead paths even if slightly slower.
- Tail latency risk areas:
  - OOM retry cascades show up as p95/p99 spikes
  - fragmentation over time if we don’t reuse buffers well

B200 (goal: bring-up + prove no regressions; ship behind flag)
- Assumption: driver/CUDA constraints; limited fleet access → canary must be strict.
- Expect different kernel sweet spots vs H100; avoid copying H100 profile blindly.
- Must have explicit fallback to H100 profile logic (or “no profile” defaults) when detection/version checks fail.

Open questions / risks
1) Hardware detection reliability
- SKU strings differ by provider; MIG shows device variants.
- Decision needed: what level of specificity in profile matching?
  - Option A: match exact SKU strings (fragile)
  - Option B: normalize into capability flags (preferred)
  - Option C: hybrid: normalized + allow exact overrides

2) Profile granularity
- Per-SKU only vs per-SKU + “modes” (balanced vs throughput-first).
- Tentative: H100 supports “balanced” and “throughput-first”; L40S likely only “balanced/safe.”

3) Compatibility + versioning
- How strict is the loader?
  - Hard fail (refuse to start) vs soft fail (warn + fall back)
- Neha preference: do not hard fail runtime start in Hosted/Dedicated; in Private we can offer a stricter mode.

4) Guardrails and safe defaults
- Need explicit “max allowed” boundaries to prevent a single profile update from bricking a pool.
- Example: never allow queue_depth > X without also enabling reject threshold; never allow kv_budget > Y on L40S.

5) Rollout + rollback semantics
- Who can flip the kill switch per pool? (SRE vs Infra vs Runtime oncall)
- We need a runbook section: “Rollback criteria” with thresholds for p95 + error rate + OOMs.

6) Benchmark suite scope and reproducibility
- What is “representative workload matrix” that won’t take 6 hours per run?
- Need smaller smoke matrix for PR gating + larger nightly matrix.

7) Documentation wording
- “Expected behavior” vs “guarantees” (Docs review note: avoid SLA language).
- Explicitly document trade-offs: throughput improvements may increase tail latency in some corner cases.

Action items (initial)
- Ethan: draft schema strawman incl. versioning + guardrails + inheritance (due 2025-11-13)
- Benji: loader precedence proposal + kill switch behavior + test plan (due 2025-11-15)
- Claire + Rina: propose workload matrix v0 + measurement methodology (due 2025-11-18)
- Sofia: propose scheduler knobs that are safe to freeze vs must remain adaptive (due 2025-11-18)
- Hiro: list kernel selection toggles + heuristic inputs we can expose safely (due 2025-11-18)
- Irene: inventory fleet variance for H100/L40S (HBM sizes, MIG usage, PCIe vs SXM prevalence) (due 2025-11-20)
- Neha: define canary rollback thresholds + required dashboards (draft) (due 2025-11-22)

Notes / parking lot
- Consider a “profile explain” CLI: dump effective config after selection + overrides (for Support + oncall).
- We should log a one-line summary at startup: “profile=h100-balanced@v0.3 (source=fleet-default) kv_budget=xx% batch_delay=yyms …”
- Need to decide how to prevent drift between runtime hard-coded defaults and profile pack defaults. Might require a normalization layer.

References (for later linking)
